values.note: 'All sites with or without water and electric are on a first come first serve basis', paid in advance to the camp hosts (517-543-3011). Up to 14 consecutive days on one site, then move to another. Checkout 3 pm. Short-term tent camping must be paid 3 days ahead and approved; no long-term tent camping. Two adults and their children per unit.

note: Transient campground at the Eaton County Fairgrounds in Charlotte, open to the public all season (closed during the July fair and certain large events) - a real all-season campground, not fair-week-only. Pick an open site and the camp hosts collect the fee. Run by the Eaton County Agricultural Society (the member fair board, not county government), so ownership recorded as private. --Claude
summary: Fair board's camping page and 2026 rules PDF: nightly camping open to the public mid-April to mid-October, $25 cash / $26 card per night (2026), water and electric hookups, dump station, restrooms and showers; phone 517-543-3011 (camp hosts) matches. Changed booking: reservable true/phone -> false, fcfs always (rules: every site first come, first served). Added the 14-consecutive-day move rule, checkout, tent limits. Amperage, site count and rig length not stated (pull-through left as derived). Note cleaned of hookups/facilities/price/booking text the fields hold.
flags: Fair-week check passes: camping is sold nightly to the public all season ('Campground open to public Mid-April to Mid-October', 'Our campground is OPEN!', $25/night), not fair-week-only. The pages do not mention closing during the fair (July 13-18, 2026); the note keeps that caveat from earlier research.

Ownership: the Eaton County Agricultural Society, 'made up of approximately 128 current members, is the governing body of the Eaton County Fair and Fairgrounds' (https://eatoncountyfair.com/pageserver/ag-society); no page says the county owns the grounds, so private stands.
